title: The Bowl of Sere and the Ten Bowls
caption: The hot southern capital three hundred leagues south of Sill, drawn as a factor's clerk at Greybank would copy a southern plan: no wall worth the name, but open courts each with a fire in the middle. The great Open Court holds the public bowl emptied at the third hour when an act of the Sun-Emperor is announced, and the fourth bowl that is set out at every feast and carried away full; nine other bowl-houses of the Ten Bowls stand about the courts. The Ember bowl-house is drawn with its fire-shrine fed with bought oil, its wine-press, its counting room no woman enters and a room with good light; Solene Ember was returned whole here in 799, 804 and 809. The grain mills stand on the cut to the south with their wheels and sacks, the grain strips and olive grounds beyond, the bond-quarters entered without a name, the trace of a broken wall, the burning winds and their yellow dust. The Peat Line runs along the north edge, where the southern advance stopped in Y.H. 634, with the road going on to Greybank and Sill. Cartouche dated Y.H. 812, the Thin Year, with compass, a scale in leagues, a convention of signs and surveyor's notes on the announced act, the mercy of the Spending, the burning of the debt-slates, the two kinds of returned stranger, the clerk's three times above the space and the Sere account with a place where a bowl should be emptied and is not.
